newsitem.title: GERMANY: German opposition says Transrapid unviable.
newsitem.headline: German opposition says Transrapid unviable.

text.p: German opposition parties said on Friday the reorganisation of the Transrapid high-speed rail project and the government's new cost and revenue projections show the planned Hamburg-Berlin route is not viable.

The departure of construction firms Phillip Holzmann AG, Hochtief AG and Bilfinger+Berger from the project shows that the project will not make money, said Elke Ferner, parliamentary transport spokeswoman for the Social Democrats (SPD).
Deutsche Bahn AG's guarantee of a return to private-sector partners is a millstone that will ultimately cost the taxpayers, Ferner said.

"This could plunge Deutsche Bahn into ruins," she said. "It is highly doubtful whether a significant portion of the 18,000 construction jobs promised by the government are created in Germany, or whether the European Union bidding procedures take them somewhere else."

Transportation Minister Mattias Wissmann told a news conference that a trimmer consortium including Thyssen AG, Siemens AG, AdTranz -- a venture between Daimler-Benz AG and ABB -- and Deutsche Bahn AG would continue the project.

But Wissmann also said the proposed Hamburg-Berlin line would require 10 percent more than the original nine-billion mark investment cost and would generate annual revenue of 790 million marks by 2010 -- down from an earlier estimate of 1.15 billion marks.

Gila Altmann, parliamentary transportation specialist for the Greens party, said Deutsche Bahn's new central role in the Transrapid could burden it with massive losses that would endanger the planned privatisation of the state-owned railway.
"This decision is senseless in transportation terms and financially crazy. The project has no future," Altmann said.

The GDED rail workers' union said today's announcements about the reorganisation of the Transrapid show the project had no vital role in German transportation policy, but that industry wanted to pursue the project as an export product.
